title: Batched in-flight eviction contracts for prefix-consistent KV cache
creator: Ari Kaplan
description:
Problem: Continuous batching and long-lived KV cache entries (prefix-scoped) create a class of races where eviction (LRU/TTL) can reclaim GPU memory that is still logically referenced by in-flight batches on the serving runtime. This leads to correctness issues (stale/missing KV leading to degraded generations), flakiness in A/B rollouts, and hard-to-reproduce production incidents.

Goal: Define and implement an eviction contract that provides deterministic correctness guarantees for prefix-aware entries under continuous batching. The contract should be lightweight (no per-token blocking in the hot path), compatible with existing LRU/TTL heuristics, and not materially worsen tail latency or memory fragmentation on GPU slabs.
acceptance_criteria: Automatic regression suite (see test_plan) detects zero KV-induced generation divergences across 1000 fuzzed prompt sequences with continuous batching enabled
End-to-end integration shows no >5% regression in p99 latency on serving 2k RPS synthetic workload compared to baseline
Eviction logs include stable audit tokens (epoch + prefix) for every reclaimed slab and pass audit verifier (no missing in-flight references)
Graceful fallback mode (TTL-only) exists and is covered by canary rollout; rollback path validated
Design doc and API changes reviewed by runtime and infra teams and sign-offs captured in comments
implementation_notes:
High level approach: 1) attach lightweight metadata to cache slots: last_access_ts, in_flight_ref_count, epoch_id, prefix_tag; 2) introduce an Eviction Intent record (EIR) persisted in the eviction coordinator for candidate slots; 3) eviction becomes a two-phase contract: ISSUE_INTENT -> WAIT_FOR_EPOCH_STABLE -> ATOMIC_RECLAIM; 4) batching epoch boundaries announce stable points so in-flight requests can decrement refcounts and publish completions; 5) use an optimistic CAS to transition a slot from INTENT to RECLAIM, preventing double-free; 6) implement a soft-quarantine reclamation where reclaimed memory goes to demotion pool for a short soft-window to reduce GPU fragmentation.

Performance primitives: keep hot-path access as a single atomic increment/decrement of in_flight_ref_count (implemented with relaxed atomics on host control plane and atomic GPU counters where necessary). Intent staging should be asynchronous and rate-limited to avoid eviction storms. For TTL-driven reclamation, convert immediate TTL expiration into an INTENT rather than immediate free; short TTLs (<5s) may bypass intent in extreme memory pressure with a special fast-path.

Trade-offs: stronger guarantees increase metadata cost and slightly more coordination; we bound impact by confining coordinator scope to shard-level and by reusing existing batching epoch announcements. If slot-level atomics become a bottleneck, we can shift to prefix-cohort counting (aggregate counters per prefix) at the cost of coarser reclamation granularity.
test_plan:
Unit tests: slot metadata transitions, CAS success/failure paths, intentional race injection.

Integration tests: synthetic continuous-batching harness that simulates typical Redwood batch sizes and variable latency backends; assert no KV misses during eviction window.

Fuzzing: extend kv-eviction-fuzzbench to inject random timing between ISSUE_INTENT and RECLAIM and validate generation outputs against a golden model.

Soak: 72-hour canary on dedicated capacity with gradual traffic ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and automatic rollback on correctness anomalies.

CI gates: regression fuzzbench must pass; p99 latency delta must be within target; code coverage for state transitions >=90%.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag gated behind kv_eviction_contract_v1. 2) Internal canary on a single dedicated pool (non-production tenants) for 48h. 3) Gradual rollout to 10% customer traffic for 24h, monitor correctness and p99. 4) If metrics stable, expand to 50% then 100% over 7 days. 5) Emergency rollback toggles available in Console and via infra runbook.

Monitoring: add eviction-intent rate, intent->reclaim latency, in_flight_ref_count histogram for live slots, and a correctness alert that fires if generation divergence >0.1% on eval set.
